messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 4167771111 — Elevated 5xx + latency observed in us-east-1 affecting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Root trigger: upstream auth/ST S latency and credential-proxy 502/504s. Paging @sara (oncall).

sara (oncall): I'm on it, joining traces and auth-proxy logs now.

kevin: Confirming spikes to sts.amazonaws.com (us-east-1). Lots of prolonged handshakes and 500s from our credential proxy -> token refresh failures.

maria: Observability shows auth hop increased by ~1-3s. End-to-end generator latency up ~300-800ms for many requests, Dedicated pools seeing elevated 5xx for token failures.

sara (oncall): Can we route traffic away from us-east-1 for non-SLA tenants? Need quick mitigation that doesn't break stateful sessions.

kevin: We can start a staged fallback. Will kick off a canary reroute for low-tier tenants: `rctl route set --region us-west-2 --weight 0.25 --filter tier:non_sla` (pseudo-command). Monitoring started.

maria: Also patching auth-proxy to increase local token cache TTL to reduce STS calls: `TOKEN_CACHE_TTL=60s` and lowering refresh concurrency. Pushing to canary hosts now.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook matched: "AWS STS regional latency". Recommended actions executed: increase token cache, enable regional fallback, reduce auth retries. Runbook link: https://runbook.example.com/sts-us-east1

product-notify: Drafted status update: "We are experiencing elevated latency and increased error rates for requests originating in AWS us-east-1 due to upstream AWS STS degradation. Mitigations in progress (regional fallback + token caching)." :warning: Posting to status page now.

kevin: Opened AWS support case #1234567890. AWS has acknowledged elevated STS latencies in us-east-1 and is investigating. Their initial guidance: route to another region for critical traffic.

maria: Observability ingest delayed ~30s; metrics and traces may be underreported. Ingest backlog currently ~15% above normal, expect gaps.

sara (oncall): Handoff plan: I'll monitor canary and stay until 21:45 UTC, handing pager to @kevin at 22:00 UTC. If canary looks good after 30m, we'll expand fallback.

kevin: Enabling dedicated-pool auth fallback (dry-run -> apply): `dedicatedctl auth-fallback --target-region us-west-2 --apply` — initiating now. Will watch for drop in 5xx.

support-engineer: Reduced retry loops (2 -> 1) and bumped circuit-breakers for heavy tenants to avoid cascading errors. Also temporarily rate-limiting large embedding jobs.

maria: Customer impact summary so far: small percentage of requests returning 5xx (token errors). Largest effect seen on high-concurrency embedding and long-chat sessions. Recommend proactive emails for top affected customers.

sara (oncall): If errors persist post-canary, we'll expand fallback to majority traffic by morning and prepare a postmortem.

kevin: Note: telemetry warnings — do not rely on short-window error rates; span ingestion is lagging. Use raw logs from proxies for accurate counts.

sara (oncall): Adding post-incident todos to the doc: preserve auth-proxy logs, collect KV cache metrics, timeline of AWS case, customer outreach drafts, and cloud-provider RCA.

incident-bot: Severity updated -> Sev2. Pager handed off to kevin at 22:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:
